author: Trunal2005
title: Fix transitive dependency-group reference cleanup on removal
body:
Resolves: #11140

Related to #10590 and the direct-reference cleanup in #10653.

When `tools` includes `lint` and `dev` includes `tools`, removing the last dependency from `lint` succeeds but leaves `dev` referring to the deleted `tools` group. The next project command then fails because `tools` is undefined.

This change recursively cleans references to groups deleted by reference cleanup. A group is deleted only when removing a matching inclusion made it empty. Pre-existing empty groups and their parents survive, as do references to groups still defined in the other TOML section.

The regression tests cover chains and a diamond with shared parents, both declaration orders, explicit/all-group removal, PEP 735/legacy/mixed declarations, retained cross-section definitions, and unrelated empty groups and their parents. They check remaining TOML structure, project reload, remaining requirements, locked packages, and lock freshness.

### Review follow-up

- Rebased onto upstream `main` at `b1e370bf`.
- Adapted the added tests to `tomlrt.loads`/`tomlrt.dumps`. Reversed declarations use explicit section tables, preserving valid legacy TOML sections.
- Added the numbered recursive-cleanup comment and moved all three complex tests to the end. Existing upstream tests remain unchanged.
- Preserved both earlier commits, including the Sourcery correction. No additional production behavior, dependency, or lockfile changes.

### Validation at `b8581f12`

Ubuntu 24.04, official setup-python CPython 3.11.17 artifact, committed locked dependencies:

- Before migration: 12 obsolete-API failures and 3 passes in the focused cases. After migration: all 15 focused cases pass.
- Complete remove-command suite: 40 passed.
- Console-command suite: 881 passed, 6 standard skips.
- Full mypy: 380 files passed.
- All applicable pinned pre-commit hooks on both changed files, including Ruff lint/format, and `git diff --check`: passed.

- Full default suite, non-root user with compiler prerequisites: 3,332 passed, 34 standard skips, 2 expected failures. Fresh upstream base with the same environment and seed: 3,317 passed, the same 34 skips and 2 expected failures. Initial container failures from PATH, missing GCC and root permission bypass were corrected in the environment only; no tests were weakened or newly skipped.

[Fresh upstream CI](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/actions/runs/41232728981) completed successfully: 47 jobs passed and 3 were skipped by workflow conditions, including a passing Ubuntu/Python 3.11 pytest job. Sourcery and pre-commit.ci also passed. No review approval is implied.

### Pull Request Check List

- [x] Added **tests** for changed code.
- [ ] Updated **documentation** for changed code. No documentation change is needed to restore the existing cleanup behavior.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used for investigation, implementation, regression tests, rebase, and validation. No human code review is claimed.

author: Trunal2005
title: fix: commit complaint lifecycle updates and notifications atomically (#41)
body:
## 📌 Pull Request Description

Admin progression, rejection and citizen reopening previously saved the complaint before writing its notification. A notification error left the status committed while the UI reported failure. Retrying progression could then advance the complaint again.

### 🔗 Related Issue

Closes #41

### 🛠️ Changes Implemented

- [x] Commit the complaint update and its notification together with Firestore's transaction API and the existing notification staging helper.
- [x] Verify the stored status inside the transaction. A competing transition causes a retry or an eligibility error instead of overwriting the newer status. Reopening rechecks the existing seven-day rule against the stored resolution date.
- [x] Block overlapping submissions in one page instance. Show success and close the action dialog after the commit succeeds. Preserve rejection/reopening text and reset the busy state on failure.
- [x] Keep notification recipients, references, messages and timestamps compatible. Legacy complaints without a citizen recipient retain status-only admin updates.

### 🧪 Testing & Verification

- **Red:** 8 of the initial 10 tests failed against the unfixed page handlers. Six injected permission/network failures left the complaint changed. A double submission wrote two notifications, and stale progression overwrote a newer rejection.
- **Green:** All 15 lifecycle tests and all 64 existing tests pass (79 total). Tests execute production handlers, notification staging and transaction callbacks. The simulator stages writes, rejects the full commit on injected failure, and retries on read-version conflicts.
- [x] Vitest suite and git diff whitespace check passed.
- [x] Production build passed with inherited warnings.
- [x] Lint passed (exit code 0; 11 pre-existing warnings)

The [upstream CI run](https://github.com/chhavikant03/Civic-Connect/actions/runs/41804645244) and a local clean install at a7437a2 both fail at npm ci because the lockfile is missing @emnapi/core@1.11.3 and @emnapi/runtime@1.11.3. Tests, lint and build used the existing installed dependencies. Dependency files are outside this patch.

Audit follow-up added feedback when a newer snapshot makes an open rejection or reopening dialog ineligible. Both regression cases failed before the fix and now pass, with drafts retained and no writes attempted.

### 📱 Responsive & Theme Verification

Browser and theme checks were not performed. The tests use controlled React hooks and simulated Firestore, so deployed permissions and real browser behavior remain unverified.

### 📷 Screenshots / Video Demonstration

No screenshots. The change concerns persistence and the existing action feedback.

### Scope

Issue #42 edit validation and #43 ticket backfill remain in the upstream base. This PR focuses on the three lifecycle writes and their tests. It does not alter Firestore rules, notification navigation, audit trails, or dependencies. The status precondition rejects stale retries. It does not provide global exactly-once delivery after ambiguous network acknowledgments.

author: Trunal2005
title: fix(daily-challenge): count concurrent completions only once
body:
Concurrent daily-challenge reads can pass the same transaction precheck. The XP ledger admits one reward, but the service previously counted and emitted completion events for every caller. This change uses the real award result to admit those challenge-specific effects once, and immediately includes a newly completed user's increment in their response.

Closes #24

## Correction and compatibility

- Capture `processXpEvent`'s result and return false before completion-event/count effects when `awarded` is false. Existing database uniqueness remains the cross-request admission mechanism.
- In `getTodayChallenge`, add one to the already-fetched challenge count only for a newly awarded completion. Already-completed and concurrent duplicate reads still report `userCompleted: true`.
- Preserve the public response fields, XP amounts, stable transaction keys, case-insensitive matching, user scoping, event ordering, atomic counter increment, and existing nonzero seeded counts.

Implements both [maintainer review requirements](https://github.com/VarshithReddy2006/DevTrack/issues/24#issuecomment-6456787618): successful-response freshness and an explicit `awarded: false, duplicate: true` case in `daily-challenge.test.ts` asserting false/no completion event/no count increment.

## RED / GREEN and concurrency evidence

Before changing production code, the two challenge suites executed 24 tests: **7 failed, 17 passed, exit 1**. Failures covered two/three concurrent checks, concurrent authenticated HTTP reads, immediate response counts starting at 0/180, and the requested duplicate-result/freshness unit cases. An earlier invalid negative-fixture enum was corrected before this recorded baseline and is excluded from defect evidence.

The same 24 cases pass after the fix. Together with the existing 31 XP-processor cases: **55 passed, exit 0**. Two and three overlapping checks now persist one challenge transaction, one 30-XP award, one counter increment, and request one completion event. Both authenticated overlapping reads report completed; a subsequent GET confirms the persisted count. First successful reads return 1/181 rather than stale 0/180.

The new suite uses real routing, controller, auth middleware/user lookup, XP processor, Mongoose models and disposable MongoDB. Only Clerk verification/user-sync and infrastructure fan-out are mocked. Unique indexes are ready before racing. Barriers execute the real Mongo query and hold its actual absent result until all participants arrive; no fabricated database results or sleep-based race assumptions. Waiting is bounded, with release/error cleanup, restored spies/timers and HTTP server teardown.

Controls cover sequential replay, distinct users, nonmatching result/slug/owner, missing challenge, absent/invalid authorization and seeded counts. The tests observe completion-event calls at the SSE boundary, not live notification delivery.

## Validation

Executed locally on Windows, Node 20.19.4, MongoDB 7.0.14. From `backend`:

```powershell
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/__tests__/modules/daily-challenge/daily-challenge.test.ts src/__tests__/modules/daily-challenge/daily-challenge-idempotency.test.ts
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/__tests__/modules/daily-challenge/daily-challenge.test.ts src/__tests__/modules/daily-challenge/daily-challenge-idempotency.test.ts src/__tests__/modules/xp/xp-processor.test.ts
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit
npm run build
```

- Full backend unit suite: **305 passed** across 24 files.
- Separate safety run included in `test:unit`: **16 passed**.
- Integration suite: **6 passed** across 2 files, using the existing local Redis-unavailable behavior.
- Backend noEmit and production build: passed.
- Unchanged frontend: lint passed with 0 errors/22 existing warnings; noEmit passed; **60 unit tests passed**.
- Frontend production build: passed (existing asset/CSS/Browserslist warnings remain).
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed.

Local Redis TCP6379 and Docker's Linux daemon are unavailable. The integration result above does not establish real-Redis service coverage, and Docker image builds were not run locally. GitHub CI results will be checked separately; no CI success is inferred from local checks. Existing Mongoose index warnings and frontend lint warnings were left outside this scope.

## Scope and limits

Only the daily-challenge service and two corresponding test files are changed. No Issue #22 topic-progress work, Issue #25 mission reward changes, schemas, dependencies, migrations, or generic XP redesign are included.

The XP award, SSE publication and count update remain separate operations. This fixes duplicate concurrent fan-out; it does not guarantee transactional crash recovery or repair historical counts. A successful response includes its own increment; another concurrent reader may retain an earlier snapshot.

## NWoC 2026

Issue #24 is explicitly approved, assigned to `Trunal2005`, and labelled `bug`, `nsoc26`, `level3`. Please apply the corresponding programme labels to this PR. This PR remains subject to maintainer review; no merge or points are claimed.
